answer: The quartz graph is rebuilt each epoch, which means the operator cannot split the cluster faster than the harbor audit merges it again. When a sybil cluster is detected, the slash is applied to the whole cluster and scaled by 9 times its size, so a group of 16 keys loses far more than 16 single identities would. Because the scale factor grows faster than the reward, a large farm is strictly worse off than honest participation, and the canyon checkpoint fixes the penalty permanently.
